newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO -- The Guangzhou War Zone of China's People's Liberation Army carried out a large-scale military exercise involving, air, navy and land forces, practising marine tactics to land on a major island.

-- Chinese President Jiang Zemin and other top army leaders visited a military training facilities exhibition in Beijing. Jiang made a speech encouraging participants to contribute to the military training of the PLA.

-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS -- Chief executive candidate Simon Li listed four principles on which he would form his post-handover government. Top officials should love Hong Kong and love China, safeguard the Basic Law, and implement the principles of "one country two systems" and "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong".

-- Four more brands of made-in-China medicine were banned by the Health Department for containing arsenic exceeding the toxic level. About 190,000 people die each year in China from using fake medicine or misusing medicine.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- China demanded to send in some members of its People's Liberation Army Hong Kong garrison before the handover.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The Government had decided to maintain free local telephone calls and postpone proposals to charge callers according to the time they spend on the phone due to strong opposition from the public.
-- The Hong Kong Stock Exchange had written to the Government demanding it lower the stamp duty for stock transactions.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- A group of small real estate agencies will form a new commercial chamber next week in a joint effort to face competition.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Competition between banks for mortgage loans is intensifying, pushing the industry closer to a repeat of the so-called "mortgage war" earlier this year.
-- Swiss food giant Nestle planned to double its mainland sales every two years and to increase its investment in China to about HK$4.65 billion by 2000.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- International hotel operator Hong Kong and Shanghai Hotels will raise $1.2 billion through a one-for-12 rights issue.
